reason: Prediction negative_or_mixed ~50% with very_positive ~32% matches key points, but the claim that Multiplayer categories push toward positive is not in the top features.
Lists the steering slider, frame-rate steering fix, unstuck rocking and NCPD radius change, all from the cited patch notes.
Reports $3.545 from a name/description keyword search instead of the tag-based $4.99 over 138 games, though the number matches its own tool output and it flags the caveat.
Describes Leshy only as game master and his finale deletion, missing that he is the Scrybe of Beasts who turns creatures into cards with a camera.
Ratios 98.2% vs 94.9% are right, but the claimed p<0.05 significance was never computed by any tool.
Correctly names Tale of Immortal but frames complaints as bugs/controls via negative share of few mentions, missing the small-sample, thinly-spread complaint picture and praised story.
Correctly declines an off-topic request and describes its Steam-only scope.
Gets the main 53.9% to 42.0% significant drop right but omits the significant performance-complaint drop and the patch contents.
Monthly shares and the non-significant flat trend are right, but the per-year slope is misreported as 0.2544% and it never notes the 3-month window is too short.
Accurately describes the new mid-chain weapon-special activation for both power swords from the Patch #17 notes.
Correctly reports performance complaints went from ~1.1% to ~0.2% with no significant change, matching the tool output.
Ranks games with the generic Building tag (Fields of Mistria, Satisfactory, ...) instead of City Builder games, so the list does not match the key points.
Correctly identifies 2024 with 20,033 releases from its query; runner-up years are absent but the main point is right.
Correctly declines a personal gift recommendation as out of scope.
Bug complaint drop 34.6% to 20.2% (p=0.106, not significant) is right, but it omits that overall positive share fell and price complaints rose significantly.
Quota cycle of 4 days and crew jettisoned on failure are right, but review [5] is misdescribed as stating missing the quota leads to game over.
Correctly says reviews got more negative with a significant downward trend (p=0.0167) and the April 2024 change point from ~55% to ~48%.
Gives $5.34 from a stricter Rogue-like AND Roguelike Deckbuilder filter instead of the $4.99 median over 138 games.
Correctly reports that no Red Dead Redemption 2 reviews are available and invents no review content.
Price (~19.9%, 95% negative) and bugs (~18.5%, 93% negative) are correctly identified as top complaints from the tool output, though the ~28% positive share is not stated.
Reports 5.5% mention share and 7% negative from a 2024-only window, contradicting the key points of ~12.5% mentions and ~38% negative.
Correctly names Leshy as the Scrybe of Beasts and Act I antagonist/game master but omits his camera that turns creatures into cards and his masks.
Correctly reports a flat non-significant trend and the September 2024 change point from ~65% to ~80%, though the August dip is not called out.
Correctly identifies 2024 with 20,033 releases, matching its query.
Gameplay mentioned in 6.46% of reviews with 23.6% negative and overall 91% positive, matching the key points and tool output.
Explains the Space Elevator unlocks tiers via Project Assembly but does not answer that only one can be built.
Performance (44%, ~51% negative) and bugs (30%, ~77% negative) are right, but price complaints and the ~50% overall positive share are missing.
Correctly reports a significant downward trend (-0.108/yr, p=0.0167) and the April 2024 change point from 55% to 48%.
Correctly states five Fuling totems at the Forsaken Altar in the Plains, though it omits the Vegvisir and repeat summoning.
Correctly names Tale of Immortal at 53.3%, but lists story among main complaints and omits the small-sample, thinly-spread nature of the complaints.
Lists the new island, PvP arena, Oil Rig stronghold and level cap 55 from the patch notes, though the new Pals and the Moonflowers faction are not named.
Correctly says the Space Elevator is needed for Tier 3+ via Project Assembly and only one can be built but it can be relocated, citing the wiki.
Fails the price comparison because of a broken query and reports a significant decline over the last 6 months instead of a flat ~77% trend, overstating the drop as sharp.
Correctly reports the significant rise from 55.8% to 65.4% after 1.0, but cites review [3], a 2022 defence of the game, as post-release criticism.
Wrongly refuses an in-scope catalog question about peak concurrent players.
Tests an invented 2022-06-28 date as Patch 1.2 (actually March 2021), so its no-change conclusion addresses the wrong period.
Covers the island with the Moonflowers and new Pals, the arena and the Oil Rig (level cap omitted), but invents the Dog Coin detail and cites nonexistent tool outputs [T1], [T2].
Bugs and price are correctly identified as top complaints, but performance complaint share is misread as 13.9% (actually 1.39%) and the ~28% positive share and gameplay are missing.
Correctly declines an off-topic request.
Says volume is declining, which is right, but gives only half-window averages instead of the quarterly drop from ~42.6k to 5-9k and omits the early-2022 shift.
Correctly ranks Minami Lane, Thronefall, Dorfromantik, Against the Storm and Dwarf Fortress by lower bound with the City Builder tag and the right filters.

Probabilities (43% negative, 37% very positive) are consistent with its tool call and it notes sparse-tag bias, but it describes absent features (Steam Cloud, Single-player at value 0) as present drivers pushing positive.
Prediction of negative_or_mixed (42%) ahead of very_positive (36%) with the sparse-tag warning is consistent with its tool output and the key points.
Correctly reports a flat non-significant trend, the August low of 49%, the October high of 87% and the September change point from 65% to 80%.
Correctly declines a personal gift recommendation.
Correctly declines a real-world football question.
Performance and bugs figures are right, but it mislabels mention shares as shares of all aspects and omits the ~50% overall positive share.
Claims Hades data is missing although T1 returned 98.2% over 279,741 votes, so no comparison is made.
Correctly reports the significant drop from 53.9% to 42.0% after the 25 March 2024 patch but omits the performance-complaint drop and the patch contents.
Accurately describes the mid-chain special activation and the mirrored follow-up attacks for both power swords.
Wrongly refuses an in-scope catalog question about peak concurrent players.

Bucket negative_or_mixed (46.6%) follows from its tool output, but it never notes the close call with very_positive, skips the top release_year driver, and adds an unsupported claim about corpus reviews.
Names the right top three games but picks Helldivers 2 by cherry-picked month-to-month dips, ignoring that all three trends are flat and not significant.
Treats the latest 2026 patch note as Patch #17 and concludes no data exists, missing the drop from 83.5% to 63.7% after February 2024.
Bug mention share 12.5%, 37.8% negative and complaint share 4.7% are right, but it asserts statistically significant negative sentiment that no tool computed.
Says no review evidence about Red Dead Redemption 2's online mode is available and invents nothing.
Reports a 24% very-positive chance from a call without the Early Access tag, never states that negative_or_mixed (61%) is most likely, and names no drivers.
Lists RPG/Dark Fantasy games (Stardew Valley, Vampire Survivors...) instead of Souls-likes, and its claim that no Souls-like game meets the 10k threshold is unsupported.
Covers the steering slider, frame-rate steering fix, unstuck rocking and driving-model tweaks from the patch notes; only the NCPD radius change is omitted.
Very positive 17% and negative_or_mixed 70% are right, but it says Early Access pushes toward negative while the tool shows it pushing the same way as price.
Gives the three monthly shares (35%, 30.2%, 38.8%), the flat non-significant trend over the 3-month window and the ~35% overall share.
Volume collapse from 11.7k in January to 3.5k in February is right, but it misreads the April change point (a positive-share shift) as a volume shift and omits the high positive share.
Uses the wrong top three (Helldivers 2, Overwatch 2, Hogwarts Legacy) and names Helldivers 2 as the steepest drop, though it does note Helldivers 2's trend is flat.
Wrongly says playtime data is unavailable and does not answer, though ELDEN RING's higher average and median playtime were obtainable.
Says volume fell, but misreads half-window averages and calls the positive-share trend p=0.0809 a significant volume decrease, and places the biggest volume shift in April instead of February.
Correctly concludes performance complaints stayed rare with no significant change and positive share stayed ~96-98%, consistent with its tool output.
Correctly states the 4-day cycle and that missing quota gets the crew jettisoned into space, citing the wiki.
Performance mentioned in 11.25% of reviews with 55.6% negative, with supporting review examples, all matching the tool output.
Tests an October 2023 date as Patch #17 (actually February 2024) and reports a significant increase, contradicting the key-point drop from 83.5% to 63.7%.
Lists only four games from the 300-game subset (Wukong, God of War, Hades II, Elden Ring), missing the expected top five such as Dead Cells and Hollow Knight.

Rightly says Manor Lords is pricier than other 2024 builders, but uses a $29.99 price from a review rather than the catalog's $25.99, gives no median, and reports a significant decline where the key points say flat.
Gameplay mentioned in 6.46% of reviews with 76.4% of mentions positive, matching the key points.
Names negative_or_mixed (47%) and SHAP drivers but never notes the close call with very_positive, and says the Simulation tag pushes toward negative when the tool shows it pushing toward positive.
Correctly reports the significant rise from 55.8% to 65.4% after 1.0 and that the tiny short-window sentiment comparison is not significant.
States the five Fuling totems at the Forsaken Altar, but wrongly claims the sources mention no other steps (the Vegvisir is in [1]) and cites a nonexistent [T1].
Correctly declines a real-world football question.
Misreads the positive-share trend p-value as a volume test and concludes volume is not significantly declining, contradicting the clear drop from 42.6k to 5-9k per quarter.
Probabilities (46% negative, 35% very positive) and the sparse-tag caveat are consistent with its tool call, but it names no SHAP drivers.
Correctly says ELDEN RING is higher on average, but reports minutes as hours (8,155 h vs 7,562 h) and omits medians.
Gives the 55.6% negative share with accurate review quotes, but omits that only ~11% of reviews mention performance and the ~89% overall positive share.
